title: Jelsa Cost Guide 2027: Daily Budget and Real Prices
metaDescription: Jelsa, Hvar costs for 2027: rooms from €50, ferries from €8.40, meals, buses and taxis, with daily budgets by season and travel style.
content:
## How Much Does a Day in Jelsa Cost?

Jelsa sits below Hvar Town on price. Stari Grad and Jelsa typically cost 20–30% less than equivalent places in Hvar Town, and village restaurants run roughly 15–20% cheaper than the waterfront in Hvar Town. Croatia-wide, daily budgets of roughly €50–75 (backpacker), €110–160 (mid-range) and €200+ (comfort) are standard in 2026 figures, and Jelsa lands at the lower end of each band.

| Style | Per person per day | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | €60–80 | Private room shared between two, bakery breakfast, one konoba meal, buses |
| Mid-range | €110–160 | Apartment or small hotel, café breakfast, restaurant dinner with wine, a boat trip or bike hire |
| Comfort | €200+ | Hotel with pool, restaurant lunch and dinner, taxis, private transfers |

These are planning figures for two people splitting the room. Solo travellers pay more, because a single traveller carries the full room cost.

## Accommodation Prices in Jelsa

Accommodation is the biggest variable, and the season changes it more than the property type does.

### Private rooms and apartments
Family-run rooms (sobe) and simple apartments cost about €40–60 per night in summer and €30–45 in shoulder season. Direct-from-owner listings in and around Jelsa, including the nearby coves of Zavala and Prapotna and the village of Vrboska, start at roughly €50–75 per night for small apartments. Larger villas near the water can start from €125 and go well above that.

### Hotels
Hotel Hvar is the best-known hotel in town. It has indoor, outdoor and salt-water pools, and its entry rates start at about €60 per night in low season. Rubin Jelsa also operates in town. Across the two open hotels, rates start around €70 in shoulder season and reach €135–170 at peak.

### Extra fees
Tourist tax is about €1–1.50 per person per night and is charged on top of the room rate. Some coastal hotels also add a €1–3 per night eco or city fee. Check whether a listed price includes these.

### Best months for value
Mid-range stays in Jelsa run about €60–100 in May, June, September and October. In July and August the same quality costs €80–140. That 25–35% gap is the easiest saving available.

## Getting to Jelsa: Ferry, Catamaran and Transfer Costs

Jelsa has no car ferry. Most visitors arrive at Stari Grad, then travel about 25 minutes by road.

- **Car ferry Split–Stari Grad (Jadrolinija line 635):** about 1 h 50 min to 2 h, several sailings a day all year. In high season (29 May–27 Sep 2026 timetable), expect about €8.40 per adult and €47.60 for a car. Off-season fares are lower, around €5.90 per adult and €35.60 for a car.
- **Catamaran line 9603 (Split–Bol–Jelsa):** about 1 h 35 min, roughly €10 in peak season and €6.40 off-season. It runs on limited days and times and sometimes routes via Stari Grad instead, so confirm the departure before booking.
- **Catamaran to Hvar Town plus bus:** about 1 h 30–1 h 40 min for the sea leg, then a bus. Fares run about €10–30 depending on operator.
- **Private boat Split to Jelsa:** about 60 minutes, from around €370 per boat. This only makes sense for groups splitting the cost.

The catamaran that calls directly at Jelsa looks like the obvious choice, but its single daily departure means a missed or rerouted sailing can leave you stranded or stuck with a taxi bill. The Stari Grad car ferry is less elegant and far more reliable, because it runs many times a day.

## Getting Around Hvar from Jelsa

- **Local buses:** Hvar Town, Stari Grad, Jelsa and Vrboska are linked by bus at roughly €3–6 per ride, depending on distance. Stari Grad to Hvar Town is about €4–5 and 20 minutes.
- **Taxis:** Fixed-route fares vary a lot. Hvar Town to Jelsa is quoted at €25–35 in some listings and up to €45–60 in others. Agree the price before getting in.
- **Car rental:** Mainland rental runs about €30–50 per day. Adding the ferry makes a car expensive for a short stay. Jelsa is compact and walkable, so a car is only worth it for exploring the island's far ends.

## Food and Drink Prices

Typical daily food spending in Jelsa for a mid-range visitor is €35–55. Rough benchmarks used for Hvar island in general, trimmed by 15–20% for village prices:

- Café breakfast: about €6–8
- Konoba lunch: about €15–20
- Mid-range dinner with wine: about €30–40 per person
- Dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant: about €60–90
- Coffee and drinks: about €6–8 per day

Self-catering cuts the bill substantially. Many Jelsa apartments include a kitchen, and a supermarket and market in town cover basics. A bakery breakfast plus one restaurant meal keeps food near €20–30 per day.

## Activities and Day Trips

Beaches around Jelsa are free to use, and the pine-shaded waterfront promenade costs nothing. Paid extras add up quickly:

- Half- or full-day boat cruises with swimming and snorkelling: about €50–100 per person, often with lunch on full-day trips.
- Island-hopping day tours: around €105 per person.
- Daily activity spending: €25–50 per person on a typical trip, less if the plan is mostly swimming and walking.

## Sample Budgets for a Week in Jelsa

| Style | Week per person (excl. flights) |
|---|---|
| Budget, shoulder season | about €385–525 |
| Mid-range | about €770–1,120 |
| Comfort, peak season | €1,400+ |

A couple staying a week in a €80 apartment in June, eating out once a day and cooking the rest, will land near €1,400–1,700 in total for the two of them including local transport.

## Money-Saving Tips for Jelsa

1. **Travel in May–June or September–October.** Prices drop 25–35% and the sea is still warm enough from June.
2. **Stay in Jelsa, not Hvar Town.** It saves €20–40 per night for similar quality, and Hvar Town is a short bus ride away.
3. **Leave the car on the mainland.** A car costs about €47.60 each way on the high-season ferry. Buses and taxis are cheaper for most stays.
4. **Book direct with owners.** Listings from local owners often undercut hotel platforms, and many allow a discount for 5–7 night stays.
5. **Eat the daily lunch menu.** Konobas away from the waterfront usually charge less than the harbour-front tables.
6. **Skip taxis on the Hvar Town run.** Taxi quotes of €25–60 for a trip that costs €3–6 by bus are rarely worth it unless you arrive after the last service.

The common advice to "just book a cheap sobe on arrival" works in May and September but fails in July and August. Good rooms near the centre sell out, and what remains is far from the sea. Book ahead for peak season.

## Is Jelsa Expensive Compared with Hvar Town?

No. Hvar Town carries the island's highest rates because of its nightlife and waterfront, while Jelsa offers comparable quality for 20–30% less. The trade-off is nightlife: Jelsa is quiet in the evening, and visitors who want clubs will spend extra on taxis or buses.

faq.question: How much does a day in Jelsa cost?
faq.answer: A budget traveller spends about €60–80 per day, a mid-range visitor €110–160, and a comfort-level traveller €200 or more. These figures assume two people sharing a room and include food and local transport.

faq.question: How much is accommodation in Jelsa per night?
faq.answer: Private rooms and simple apartments cost about €45–65 in summer and €30–45 in shoulder season. Hotels start near €70 in shoulder season and reach €135–170 at peak. Tourist tax of about €1–1.50 per person per night is extra.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Split to Jelsa?
faq.answer: There is no car ferry to Jelsa itself. The Split–Stari Grad ferry costs about €8.40 per adult and €47.60 for a car in high season, followed by a roughly 25-minute road transfer. The Jadrolinija catamaran direct to Jelsa costs about €6.40–10, but it runs on limited days.

faq.question: Is Jelsa cheaper than Hvar Town?
faq.answer: Yes. Accommodation in Jelsa is typically 20–30% cheaper for comparable quality, saving €20–40 per night. Restaurants in village settings are about 15–20% cheaper.

faq.question: How much is a taxi from Hvar Town to Jelsa?
faq.answer: Quotes range from about €25–35 to €45–60 depending on the operator and time. Agree a fixed price in advance. The bus costs only about €3–6 per ride.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time to visit Jelsa?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October cost 25–35% less than July and August. Mid-range stays run about €60–100 in shoulder season against €80–140 at peak.

faq.question: Do you need a car in Jelsa?
faq.answer: No. The town is compact and walkable, and buses link it to Hvar Town, Stari Grad and Vrboska. A car adds about €35.60–47.60 each way in ferry fees, so it only pays off for exploring the whole island.

quickAnswer: Jelsa is one of the cheaper bases on Hvar. Plan on €60–80 per person per day on a budget, €110–160 mid-range, and €200+ for comfort. Private rooms start around €45–65 a night, hotel rooms run €70–170 depending on season, and the Split ferry costs about €8.40 on foot.
